subject: Issues on HPC Centos 7 Conda environment: "Instruction not allowed (core dumped)"

messages.author: 9a5b747b943f32d3
messages.subject: Issues on HPC Centos 7 Conda environment: "Instruction not allowed (core dumped)"
parts:
Dear INLA discussion group,

I recently had to switch from HPC and I have been facing issues in running R INLA since then.  Given the available modules/libraries and the user rights, I have no choice but to use Conda environments.

I managed to successfully install R 4.2.2 and R INLA (latest test version, binary build for Centos7) but the working example from the website yields the following error message:

sh : ligne 1 : 4684 Instruction not allowed (core dumped) '/home/supplisson/.conda/envs/RINLA/lib/R/library/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/inla. mkl.run' -s -v -t16:1 -B0 -P compact '/tmp/RtmpJRNCI0/filef977153d4cd/Model.ini' > '/tmp/RtmpJRNCI0/filef977153d4cd/Logfile.txt'.

I don't think there is any issue with my R installation per se since I get no error when installing/loading R INLA (I have tried multiple times) and basics examples for rjags and bmrs/stan are working. However, if this can be of any help, I installed these packages through the Conda command and R-INLA directly through install.packages (the last version on Conda is 2 years old).

Has anyone had a similar problem before and could give me a hand? I am a beginner in HPC/Linux so I may have missed an easy fix.

Cheers,
Olivier

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Issues on HPC Centos 7 Conda environment: "Instruction not allowed (core dumped)"
parts:
On Sun, 2023-01-08 at 15:06 -0800, Olivier Supplisson wrote:
> sh : ligne 1 : 4684 Instruction not allowed (core dumped)

and this shell-script says

#!/bin/bash

maybe there is something there? you might need some linux-qualified
help. I think this is just a tiny detail that needs to be fixed.

you can also try with

inla(y ~ 1, data=data.frame(y=0), verbose=TRUE, safe=FALSE, debug=TRUE)

until you figure this out.



its not related to R. this is (pure) linux. R starts a shell-script
which set up environmental variables and then run the inla-program

let me know...
Best
H

--

Dear Professor Rue,

Thank you very much for your reply on this issue.

After investigating the problem with the HPC team, it was due to nodes with obsolete Linux kernels.

They solved the issue by creating a specific module at the HPC level. I don't have more details to share beyond that, I am sorry.

Best,
Olivier
